standard_prerequisites.name: Finite-dimensional strong cone avoidance
standard_prerequisites.statement: Wang strong cone avoidance for fixed-arity free sets; Cholak-Patey strong cone avoidance for the achromatic Ramsey theorem at the Catalan bound C_n. Both cited classical statements are supplied verbatim.

standard_prerequisites.name: Effective compactness and countable forcing
standard_prerequisites.statement: König compactness for finitely branching trees, Sigma01(X) enumeration, and constructing a descending chain meeting countably many dense requirements.

core_obligations: Construct a forcing with a finite stem, cone-avoiding reservoir and extensible progressive coloring; stabilize finitely many boundary interactions using finite-dimensional cone avoidance and Catalan bounds.
Replace the noncompact coloring space by a compact relation coding, giving a finitary forcing question and extensions meeting its positive and negative specifications.
Diagonalize against each Turing functional while growing the stem, then combine the density requirements to obtain an infinite free set avoiding the prescribed cone, with relativization to Z.
difficulty_reason: Finite-arity cone avoidance does not preserve a free set for a variable-size domain. The proof creates new forcing conditions and a compact relation coding to manage arbitrary colorings while retaining diagonalization against the forbidden cone.

compared.difference: Public585-587 reduces all fixed-arity free-set instances to the large free-set problem; none of the new target reduction/coding/cone-avoidance conclusions is that statement.

Existing task719-728 codes the omega jump via thin sets on the fixed Schreier barrier. These targets respectively construct a binary Ramsey reduction, a progressive halting-code barrier, or a cone-avoiding forcing. Shared finite-jump support is not counted separately.

dedup.scope: Current manifest source/primary locator, all existing P Schreier tasks and retired source matching; direct corollaries excluded.

editorial_notes: The coloring f need not be Z-computable. The bounding function h is Z-computable; this distinction is essential to strong cone avoidance.

All new forcing conditions, stabilization/extension lemmas, relation coding, specification and diagonalization arguments are included in the solution. No forcing lemma is supplied as a free prerequisite.
The target is the progressive-coloring theorem itself. Its rainbow corollary and finite-dimensional special cases are not counted separately.

editorial_scope: One original result. Full source-local mathematical construction included; named classical inputs are explicit.
